restoration_note: Teaching defines Greatness as the bearing-realm (Great Land) and Father as the first-establishing source within it, then iterates this Father–Greatness pattern across discrete degrees: inmost Father, Third Ambassador, Jesus the Radiance, Pillar of Glory, five holy gods. The iterated formula 'they call X Father; his Greatness is Y, the rooted-one within him, established beneath him' constrained nearly every restoration with high confidence. Editor restorations were accepted across the board where they reproduced this formula. Corrected {11}: text shows ⲡⲉⲁ̄ partial → completing to ⲡⲉⲁⲩ 'glory' requires ⲩ, not editor's ⲗ. Two gaps left unrestorable: {14} (5-char noun describing the five gods, multiple equally-plausible candidates including ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄/ⲡⲉⲁⲩ/ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ) and {18} (12-char clausal close with only the ⲩⲉ trace as anchor — too many syntactic options).

restorations.basis: Genitive linker completing 'Father of the Greatness' as the cited title; matches ⲡⲓⲱⲧ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ in line 9 verbatim.
Same genitive linker as gap 0; the question 'Father of the Greatness — for what reason?' parallels ch.20.9.

Copula + postposed-subject marker fits 'the one established firmly in him is, namely the substance of Light'; ~6 chars matches estimate; ⲛ̄ϭⲓ is the standard Coptic device for delayed nominal subject after a relative clause.

Plural circumstantial with totalizer fits the antecedent 'all the rich ones, the angels, and dwelling-places'; ~11 chars matches estimate; participle ⲥⲙⲁⲛⲧ requires a circumstantial subject before it.
Editor restoration confirmed: ⲧⲧⲁⲗⲓⲛ ⲁⲛ is the iteration-marker between formula members; ϣⲁⲩⲙ joins the visible ⲟⲩⲧⲉ to make ϣⲁⲩⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ 'they call.'

Editor restoration confirmed; reproduces the formula 'Father, his Greatness is X' verbatim from the inmost-Father stanza, with X here = the Vessel of Light of Living Fire (the Ambassador's bearing-realm).
Editor restoration confirmed; ⲡⲉⲧϩⲟⲩⲏⲥ … ⲉϥⲥⲙⲁⲛⲧ ⲛⲥⲏⲧϥ ('rooted in him, established beneath him') is the fixed paired-relative formula attested at ch.20.13–14 and ch.20.21–22.
Editor restoration confirmed; iteration-marker plus ⲓⲏⲥ ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ (Jesus the Radiance) per the lexicon entry, fitting the visible ⲡⲧⲡⲣⲉ.
Editor restoration confirmed; ϣⲁⲩⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ ⲁⲣⲁϥ 'they call him' is the standard Lycopolitan idiom, used identically at ch.20.4 and ch.20.12.
Editor restoration confirmed; ⲧⲉϥⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ ('his Greatness') is the recurring formula across the stanza, identifying the abode-of-counsels as the Radiance's bearing-realm.
Editor restoration confirmed; opening verb of each formula-member ('they also call X 'Father, his Greatness…'').
Correcting editor's 'ⲗ': lexicon entry for Pillar of Glory is ⲡⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ ⲙ̄ⲡⲉⲁⲩ; the visible ⲡⲉⲁ̄ trace requires only final ⲩ to complete ⲡⲉⲁⲩ 'glory.'
Editor restoration confirmed; ⲧⲉϩⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ 'his Greatness' identical to the formula at ch.20.18 and ch.20.21 — the Pillar's Greatness is the path of ascent itself.
6-char iteration-marker matching the openings of prior formula-members at ch.20.17 and ch.20.20; fits estimated character count exactly; the verb ϣⲁⲩⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ is implied or has fallen out.

5-char genitive complement of 'the five gods of [N], the holy ones': candidates ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄ ('life'), ⲡⲉⲁⲩ ('glory'), and ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ ('light') all fit the spiritual sense but Coptic length and corpus parallels do not single one out. Honest non-restoration.
Editor restoration confirmed; completes ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲃⲉ 'holy' from the visible ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲃ̄ trace.
Editor restoration confirmed; ⲛⲉⲧⲟⲩⲏⲥ (Lycopolitan plural of ⲡⲉⲧϩⲟⲩⲏⲥ 'rooted-one') opens the recurring 'rooted, established beneath' clause that closes each formula-member.
Editor restoration confirmed; completes ⲛⲉⲧⲟⲩⲏⲥ + ⲉⲧⲥⲙⲁⲛⲧ ⲛⲥⲏⲧⲟⲩ — the plural form of the iterated 'rooted in him, established beneath him' formula now applied to the five gods.

12-char closing clause with only ⲩⲉ as visible trace; multiple syntactic options remain plausible (e.g., ⲡⲉⲩⲉⲓⲱⲧ ⲡⲉ ⲥⲱⲟⲩ 'their father is, likewise' or ⲙⲟⲩⲧⲉ ⲁⲣⲁⲩⲉ ⲭⲉ ⲓⲱⲧ 'they call them Father'), and neither is uniquely constrained by formula. Honest non-restoration preferred to invention.
